projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The sustained presence of 19–26 devices combined with zero camera motion suggests either a network reporting anomaly or a large gathering confined to a single area without camera coverage. This matters because it could mask actual activity or indicate a network issue that needs verification.

The network shows 19-26 connected devices over the last four hours with zero camera motion, strongly indicating a social gathering or guests are present rather than a typical family evening. This context is important for accurate security monitoring and activity logging.

The consistent presence of 19-24 devices over four hours combined with zero camera activity is highly unusual for an occupied home with children and dogs, strongly suggesting the camera system may be offline, malfunctioning, or in a non-recording mode, creating a security blind spot.

The stable 21-24 device count paired with zero camera activity and consistent presence confirms a stationary scenario, likely indicating guests or a localized tech session rather than a security event, aligning with typical weekday afternoon downtime.

The sustained 21-23 device count combined with zero camera activity on a weekday afternoon strongly indicates a presence detection glitch or misclassification of IoT devices as phones, rather than actual occupancy. Steve should audit his network's device list to prevent false automations or unnecessary alerts.

The sustained presence of 21-25 mobile devices paired with zero camera triggers on a weekday afternoon strongly indicates a large, quiet gathering or event is underway, as normal household activity would typically activate at least one motion sensor or doorbell camera.

The persistent 22-25 device count combined with zero camera activity on a weekday afternoon strongly suggests either a camera system malfunction or that cameras were deliberately disabled during a gathering, warranting immediate verification to rule out security or system issues.

The persistent 23-25 connected mobile devices strongly suggests a large gathering or extended family visit, but the complete lack of camera activity during this high-occupancy period indicates a potential monitoring blind spot or disabled cameras that should be verified.

The persistent 23-25 device count paired with zero camera activity on a weekday morning strongly indicates the home is unoccupied, with the high count likely stemming from stationary IoT hubs or guest devices rather than the family. This warrants verifying camera functionality and confirming the household's whereabouts.

The network reports 23-25 mobile devices home with zero camera activity on a weekday morning, strongly suggesting IoT devices are being misclassified as phones or there is a network reporting glitch rather than actual visitors.
